C5.label: unsupported
C5.reason: evidence bears on the claim but no supporting argument was built
C5.text: Northern Virginia data centres account for less than half of projected local peak-load growth through 2030.

C10.label: unsupported
C10.reason: evidence bears on the claim but no supporting argument was built
C10.text: Excluding new dispatchable generation, PJM's available accredited capacity remains unchanged through 2030 as resource gains offset losses.

C13.label: unsupported
C13.reason: evidence bears on the claim but no supporting argument was built
C13.text: Without new dispatchable generation, PJM's projected accredited capacity exactly meets its resource-adequacy requirement throughout the planning period through 2030.

C16.label: defeated
C16.reason: all constructed support is out, withdrawn or inapplicable
C16.text: Without new dispatchable generation, existing transmission can deliver projected Northern Virginia data-centre load through 2030 while meeting applicable reliability criteria; no transmission upgrades are required.

C20.label: accepted
C20.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C20.text: Synapse's Advanced Policy portfolio, including 9 GW of new gas, has modeled PJM-wide LOLE of 0.04 days in 2030.

C22.label: accepted
C22.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C22.text: The Pennsylvania study's Reference scenario reports PJM-wide LOLE of 0.59 days in 2030 despite modeled gas additions and data-centre flexibility.

C23.label: accepted
C23.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C23.text: The Maryland OPC records transmission projects proposed to address reliability needs associated with Northern Virginia data centres.

C24.label: accepted
C24.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C24.text: PJM states that data centres account for most of the Dominion forecast adjustment in its breakout of data-centre and voltage-reduction effects.

C25.label: accepted
C25.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C25.text: PJM's 2026 forecast requires firm commitments for near-term large-load adjustments and derates longer-term non-firm projects for uncertainty.

C26.label: accepted
C26.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C26.text: Dominion's forecast submission averages high and low statistical scenarios and is checked against executed contracts; engineering agreements are not classified as firm load.

C28.label: accepted
C28.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C28.text: The Pennsylvania adequacy study converts PJM large-load peak forecasts to annual energy using a flat load shape and cannot separate Dominion data centres from voltage optimization.

C29.label: accepted
C29.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C29.text: The Pennsylvania study's No New Data Centers scenario removes incremental data-centre load from 2027 onward; its flat demand is an assumption, not a finding of no expected growth.

C30.label: accepted
C30.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C30.text: Synapse's Status Quo scenario assumes roughly 8 GW of demand response through 2030; Advanced Policy assumes DERs and demand response reduce peak load by about 31 GW.

C31.label: accepted
C31.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C31.text: Synapse assumes Dominion offshore wind is completed by 2030; other advanced-energy builds are economically selected within queue-based limits, not guaranteed additions.

C32.label: accepted
C32.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C32.text: PJM's ELCC study administratively assumes a capacity benefit of external ties of 1.5%; this is not a quantified commitment of firm imports through 2030.

C33.label: accepted
C33.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C33.text: PJM's ELCC portfolios include planned resources, assumed external firm transactions and demand resources; later-year additions and retirements use a vendor forecast.

C34.label: accepted
C34.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C34.text: The Pennsylvania study assumes scheduled thermal retirements, allows earlier economic retirement, and assumes Three Mile Island Unit 1 returns in summer 2027.

C36.label: accepted
C36.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C36.text: The Pennsylvania report's Reference and High Load and Low Supply scenarios exceed PJM's LOLE criterion in every modeled year; both add gas.

C37.label: accepted
C37.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C37.text: Synapse's Status Quo and Advanced Policy portfolios report LOLE above and below PJM's criterion, respectively; both include new gas.

C38.label: accepted
C38.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C38.text: The Maryland OPC report records BGE's request for incentives for an estimated $634 million of transmission projects addressing Northern Virginia data-centre reliability needs in the 2022 RTEP.

C39.label: accepted
C39.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C39.text: The Pennsylvania resource-adequacy report allows unrestricted within-zone transfers and defines adequacy outages as generation shortages, not transmission or distribution outages.

C40.label: accepted
C40.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C40.text: Synapse's Advanced Policy scenario permits economic advanced transmission additions from 2028; that permission is not a committed Northern Virginia upgrade schedule.

C41.label: accepted
C41.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C41.text: PJM's ELCC and reserve analysis models the RTO as an isolated area without internal transmission constraints; its results do not test Northern Virginia deliverability.

C42.label: accepted
C42.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C42.text: Synapse's Advanced Policy scenario assumes a 17 percent PJM peak reduction in 2030 from DERs including demand response, with some flexibility participating in emergency load response.

C43.label: accepted
C43.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C43.text: The Pennsylvania assessment assumes Reference-case flexibility of 13 percent of peak data-centre load during 0.50 percent of annual hours, using stress-hour demand shifting without reducing annual energy.

C44.label: accepted
C44.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C44.text: PJM attributes higher demand-response accreditation for 2027/28 to removing its performance window and treating demand response as available around the clock; winter capability remains a rating constraint.

C45.label: accepted
C45.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C45.text: PJM's Table 4 reports a 12,804 MW UCAP shortfall for delivery year 2029/2030 under its vendor-forecast portfolio, comparing 148,375 MW of accredited UCAP with a 161,179 MW requirement. This is a table balance, not a measure of capacity actually procurable in RPM: capacity-interconnection-rights limits can further reduce available offers.

C46.label: accepted
C46.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C46.text: PJM's ELCC study reports Table 4 UCAP shortfalls of 4,189 MW in delivery year 2028/2029 and 12,804 MW in 2029/2030 under its vendor-forecast portfolios. The totals include assumed external firm capacity purchases and sales, and the requirements incorporate an administratively assumed emergency-import capacity benefit of ties; these are not import-independent adequacy findings.

C47.label: defeated
C47.reason: all constructed support is out, withdrawn or inapplicable
C47.text: Modo states that Dominion data centres account for most of its projected PJM coincident-peak increment from 2029 to 2030. This records Modo's attribution, not a validated demand forecast or an estimate of Northern Virginia's cumulative local peak-load growth.
